messages:
Carmen: Hey folks — quick one. I have a scheduled outpatient procedure on 2026-12-28 that overlaps the year-end shutdown. Im not sure whether to use PTO, sick, or request a blackout exemption. Any guidance?
Dana - People Ops: Thanks for asking, Carmen. For medical procedures that are scheduled by the employee, we generally expect use of sick time or PTO depending on your local sick policy. Blackout exemptions are reserved for employer-mandated or legally protected leaves. :spiral_calendar:
Carmen: Got it. Is there any protection if the procedure causes me to exceed the carryover cap? Id lose a day of carryover otherwise.
Dana - People Ops: We're flexible here. If the procedure is medically necessary and you provide documentation (clinic appointment confirmation or surgeon note), we can either: 1) mark the shutdown days as protected medical absence (so they dont count against carryover) OR 2) allow one-time carryover exception for the affected accrual year. Upload docs to the HR portal or email people-ops@redwood.ai with subject "Medical blackout request - Carmen".
Tom (Eng Manager): Carmen — I can approve PTO for travel/recovery days around the procedure if you prefer paid days. Also happy to reassign on-call.
Carmen: Thanks Tom. If I submit a sick-day, do I need to specify recovery vs procedure in the reason?
Dana - People Ops: Short answer: no, just mark as "sick - medical procedure" in AbsencePortal. If you want the blackout protection route, include the clinic note and request protection in the email; we will treat those shutdown dates as medical-protected after verification.
payroll-bot: Reminder: If People Ops marks dates as protected medical absence, payroll will reconcile accruals on the next payroll run. Any company-paid supplements (e.g., short-term disability offsets) will be coordinated via Payroll.
Carmen: One follow-up  will short-term disability paperwork block the blackout exemption? I might apply after recovery.
Dana - People Ops: No, theyre separate. Blackout protection for scheduled medical dates is independent of STD claims. You can request the blackout protection now and pursue STD later. People Ops will coordinate with Payroll and Benefits as needed.
people-ops-bot: Ticket created: PO-8123. Please attach appointment confirmation or clinical note. Expect review in 2 business days.
Carmen: Uploaded appointment confirmation and emailed people-ops@redwood.ai (subject: "Medical blackout request - Carmen"). Thanks everyone.
Tom (Eng Manager): Let me know if you want tentative PTO approved for recovery days. I can sign off quickly so calendars are accurate.
Carmen: Appreciate it  doing the upload now. :pray:
file_notes: medical procedure during year-end shutdown - sick vs PTO vs blackout
